title: Micro-Fidelity Migration and Hybrid Pricing Playbook
author: Ava Patel
content:
Summary:

This playbook provides a step-by-step operational and commercial plan for migrating customers from coarse-grained token billing and large-bundle fidelity SKUs to a micro-fidelity, hybrid-pricing model. The goal is to reduce friction for mid-market customers migrating from hosted to Dedicated or Private deployments while protecting Redwood economics and preserving predictable unit costs.

Audience:
- Product managers owning pricing and packaging
- Solutions Engineers / Sales Engineers executing migrations
- Account teams for customer communications
- Finance for revenue recognition impacts
- Billing & metering engineers for implementation details

Objectives:
- Provide a repeatable migration path with playbook steps and run rates.
- Define a hybrid pricing construct that combines base capacity + micro-fidelity credits.
- Ensure observability signals and guardrails to detect revenue or quality regressions.
- Offer recommended incentives and temporary discounts for migrations.

Background and motivation:
Many mid-market customers rely on bundled token credits and per-tenant fidelity SKUs that are inflexible for incremental usage patterns. Customers hesitate to commit to Dedicated capacity without a predictable marginal cost for higher-fidelity requests. The micro-fidelity model decomposes fidelity (compute/latency/quality) into small, billable credit units customers can attach per-route or per-model.

High-level hybrid pricing model (recommended):
- Base reservation: monthly committed capacity (vCPU/GPU units) with guaranteed throughput SLA.
- Included credit bucket: X micro-fidelity credits/month (consumed first).
- On-demand micro-credits: per-1k-token equivalent credit price for bursts and higher-fidelity model variants.
- Fallback pricing: guaranteed cost ceiling via auto-fallback to standard model variants when on-demand credit spend would exceed configured monthly cap.

Core micro-credit definitions and examples:
- Micro-fidelity credit (MFC): unit that maps to compute/latency premium for a request. 1 MFC ~= baseline for 1k standard tokens at standard quality.
- Example tiers: low-fidelity = 0.25 MFC/1k tokens, standard = 1 MFC/1k tokens, premium = 3 MFC/1k tokens.

Sample pricing table (examples for guidance only):
| Component | Metric | Pricing example | Notes |
|----------|--------:|----------------:|-------|
| Base reservation | GPU-hour equivalent | $12,000 / month | 1x p3.2xlarge equivalent; guaranteed 95th %-ile latency SLO |
| Included credits | MFC / month | 100,000 MFC | Applies across tenant; resets monthly |
| On-demand MFC | MFC / 1k tokens | $0.0009 / MFC | Metered at request time |
| Cost ceiling | Monthly spend cap | Customer-configured | Auto-fallback triggers at cap |

Migration playbook (sales + SE + engineering):
1) Pre-migration audit (SE + account):
   - Collect current token usage: 7-day, 30-day, and 90-day histograms by route and model.
   - Collect peak concurrency and latency-sensitive routes.
   - Identify top 10 prompt templates driving premium fidelity.
   - Deliver a migration readiness score (green/amber/red).
2) Plan and propose (SE + product + finance):
   - Map historical usage to MFC consumption using conversion factors (use 1 MFC/1k tokens baseline; adjust for model variants).
   - Propose a base reservation sized for 75th percentile baseline throughput.
   - Propose included credits at 40% of expected monthly MFC burn to encourage predictable commit.
   - Simulate monthly cost under 3 consumption scenarios (conservative, expected, high). Attach example spreadsheet export.
3) Pilot (2–4 weeks):
   - Enable micro-credit meter in a sandpit tenant.
   - Route 20% of traffic to micro-fidelity-priced variants with observability flags.
   - Capture quality metrics (BLEU-like scoring, embedding drift, or customer-specific evals).
   - Validate billing events and invoice lines in staging billing pipeline.
4) Full migration rollout (4–8 weeks):
   - Gradual ramp: 20% -> 50% -> 100% traffic shift with checkpoints.
   - Enable cost ceiling auto-fallback and alerting for >10% variance vs forecast.
   - Apply any agreed migration credits or temporary discounts as contract adjustments.
5) Post-migration evaluation (30/60/90 days):
   - Review MFC utilization, cost per 1k tokens, and customer quality SLAs.
   - Update recommended included credit levels and reserved capacity if patterns diverge.

Implementation requirements (billing & metering):
- Metering lane must emit per-request MFC usage with the following fields: tenant_id, route, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, mfc_consumed, timestamp.
- Billing pipeline must support aggregation by tenant-month and export a line-item per MFC category.
- Console must display three cost projections: current month burn, forecast at current rate, and worst-case cap.
- Audit logs for migration promotions and discount adjustments.

SLOs, observability & alerts:
- Billing accuracy: <0.1% reconciliation drift between meter and invoice for migrated accounts (30-day rolling).
- Quality regression: customer-specific eval A/B delta no worse than -2% from baseline for the first 30 days.
- Cost variance: alert if monthly spend > 15% above pilot forecast within first 60 days.
- Latency SLO: reserved capacity routes maintain 95th %-ile latency below target (per-customer SLO).

Incentives and commercial constructs:
- Migration credit: one-time 10% MFC top-up applied first month for eligible mid-market customers.
- Ramp discount: first 3 months, on-demand MFCs billed at 90% list for customers that commit to a 6-month base reservation.
- Quality credits: conditional refunds if measured quality metrics drop below agreed thresholds after migration (per contract).

Risk register and mitigations:
- Risk: Unexpectedly high MFC burn increases customer churn.
  Mitigation: Cost ceiling auto-fallback and pre-migration simulations; clear comms on estimated worst-case spend.
- Risk: Billing disputes due to meter mismatch.
  Mitigation: Pilot reconciliation, invoice preview, and 30-day dispute SLA handled by billing ops.
- Risk: Customer perceives complexity.
  Mitigation: Offer a managed migration option (SE-led) and pre-packaged migration templates.

Rollout timeline and milestones (quarterly cadence):
- Q4 2026: Billing pipeline MVP and console cost projections.
- Q1 2027: Pilot with 5 mid-market customers and refine conversion factors.
- Q2 2027: Launch public pricing page and self-serve migration templates.
- Q3 2027: Expand to Dedicated and Private deployments; add on-prem metering connector.

Ownership and contacts:

- Migration operations: Solutions Engineering (Sana Mehta)
- Billing & metering implementation: Eng infra (Diego Ramirez)

Appendix A — Example conversion logic (pseudocode):
- baseline_mfc = tokens_k * variant_multiplier
- variant_multiplier examples: {"low": 0.25, "standard": 1.0, "premium": 3.0}
- apply_customer_adjustment = baseline_mfc * customer_quality_factor

Appendix B — Example console screenshots (text descriptions):
- Billing preview panel: shows included credits, month-to-date MFC burn, forecast, and cap slider.
- Migration dashboard: per-route MFC burn heatmap, top 5 prompt templates by spend, quality delta sparkline.
